frequency_question: How often does an emerging market central bank initiate a rate hike within a 15-month window during similar macroeconomic recovery phases?
membership_rule: Includes any sovereign emerging market central bank policy rate cycle starting a hiking phase after at least six months of stable or declining rates; excludes advanced economies and emergency overnight interventions during acute panic.
provenance_note: claims 10 cases from only 3 named (3.3x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: 6 named or grouped major instances; estimated approximately 10 relevant systemic episodes globally in the last decade.
known_gaps: Excludes smaller frontier markets with idiosyncratic peg structures.
skeleton: Three major emerging market hiking cycles initiated out of protracted holds across a universe of roughly 10 comparable systemic emerging market central bank jurisdictions over a multi-year post-pandemic normalization window.
multiplier: 3 observed tightening initiations across comparable systemic peers during global inflationary pressures
validity_reason: Structural central bank reaction functions to inflation and global Fed cycles evolve slowly over multi-year horizons.
